title: Low-volume 12-hour selloff reversal on 1h: buy drops not backed by volume, 12-hour time exit

source.title: Trading Volume and Liquidity Provision in Cryptocurrency Markets (Bianchi, Babiak, Dickerson, CERGE-EI WP 730 / JBF 2022)

rule_summary: 1h closed bars; signal at bar close t, fill at next open; long only, one position, no pyramiding. r12(t) = close(t)/close(t-12) - 1. s12(t) = sample std of 1h log returns over bars t-720..t-1 times sqrt(12). V12(t) = sum of volume over bars t-11..t. Vmed(t) = median of the 60 non-overlapping 12-bar volume sums V12(t-12), V12(t-24), ..., V12(t-720) (prior 30 days, current window excluded). ENTRY at close of t when ALL hold: r12(t) <= -1.0*s12(t); r12(t) <= -0.015; V12(t) < Vmed(t) (the drop happened on below-median volume); no open position. EXIT, first of: close >= close(t-12) of the signal bar (move fully retraced; exit next open); stop at entry*0.95 (intrabar); time exit at the open 12 bars after entry.
mechanism: Bianchi, Babiak and Dickerson show that in crypto the interaction of past returns and volume predicts reversals: price moves on low volume reflect liquidity demand rather than information and revert, rewarding liquidity providers for inventory risk (CXO Advisory's summary describes the 12-hour horizon and the low-volume condition). The seller on the other side is an impatient trader pushing price through a thin book; with no information behind the move, the price comes back. The lab already tested the high-volume selloff (H-050); this is the opposite volume condition and a different mechanism. Entry needs at least a 1.5% drop, so a partial retrace of the drop is worth roughly 0.8% or more gross, above the round-trip cost.
